newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SPANISH SEED MANTILLA CRUISES PAST WASHINGTON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPANISH SEED MANTILLA CRUISES PAST WASHINGTON.

text.p: Fourteenth seed Felix Mantilla became the second Spaniard through to the men's quarter-finals at the Australian Open on Sunday when he beat MaliVai Washington of the United States in straight sets.
Mantilla defeated last year's Wimbledon finalist Washington 7-5 6-2 6-1 in one hour and 42 minutes with a convincing display from the baseline.
The 22-year-old will meet compatriot Carlos Moya in the quarter-finals for a baseline duel set to transfix Barcelona, the northern Spanish city where both men live.
Moya, who beat Boris Becker in the first round of the tournament, beat Sweden's Jonas Bjorkman in five sets in an earlier fourth round tie on Sunday.
Another Spaniard, 10th seed Albert Costa, plays his fourth round match against South African Wayne Ferreira on Monday.
